title: Deterministic Dedicated Throughput Validation Probe
creator: Asha Patel
description: Ship a reproducible, deterministic load-probing harness and a customer-facing acceptance kit for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. This ticket covers: 1) a probe runner that can synthesize traffic shapes derived from customer traces and deterministic RNG seeds so runs are reproducible; 2) a scenario composer that models KV-cache warmup, prefix caching, and mixed request sizes (short chat-turns + long completions); 3) autoscaling trigger simulation and verification (scale-up/scale-down thresholds, cooldowns, burst policies); 4) integration with Console dashboards for per-run artifact collection (latency histograms, tail trends, token accounting) and 5) a compact customer-run acceptance checklist and runbook that customers can execute to validate their committed throughput with minimal Redwood support. The intent is to provide an executable golden-file style run that both engineering and customers can re-run to verify throughput SLAs and uncover regressions between runtime releases.
acceptance_criteria: Probe produces byte-for-byte identical synthetic request sequences given the same seed and scenario configuration
Recorded run artifacts (token counts, latency histograms, error traces) upload to Console and are queryable by run-id
Automated check verifies committed throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) sustained for configurable windows (default 10m) within +/-10% of expected for at least three independent runs
Autoscaling policies triggered in the harness mirror production behavior (scale events emitted, cooldowns respected) and documented in the run report
Customer-facing acceptance checklist and one-click script exist and have been validated with at least two beta customers
tasks: Design deterministic scenario schema (seed, request distribution, KV-warmup steps, batching hints)
Implement probe runner as a Go binary with modes: local, k8s-job, customer-script
Add scenario-to-real-trace mapper to translate p95/p50 request sizes and inter-arrival times into synthetic workloads
Hook artifact uploads to Console: latency histograms (per-token and per-request), token accounting, autoscaler events
Create customer acceptance checklist and minimal runbook (CLI + k8s job YAML + expected artifact URLs)
E2E test: run probe against staging dedicated fleet and validate reproducibility across 5 runs

notes: This probe is intentionally opinionated: it enforces a seed-first model so we can compare runs across runtime releases. Key trade-offs: we prioritize reproducibility over perfectly emulating bursty human traffic; customers can supply a trace mapper to match their exact profile. Long-term this harness becomes part of the Dedicated capacity certification pipeline and the pre-upgrade gating checks.
